name: Vildagliptin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Vildagliptin exposure roughly doubles in severe kidney impairment, and its inactive main metabolite accumulates more. The European label keeps 100 mg/day (50 mg twice daily) at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 50 mL/min or above and uses 50 mg once daily for moderate or severe impairment and end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), including hemodialysis. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: European summary of product characteristics (SmPC) uses creatinine clearance (CrCl, mL/min); cut-off 50 mL/min.

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 50 mg twice daily (100 mg/day); 50 mg once daily in the morning when combined with a sulfonylurea. Maximum 100 mg/day (SmPC).
CrCl ≥50: no adjustment (50 mg twice daily). CrCl <50 (moderate impairment): 50 mg once daily (SmPC).

hd.text: ESKD on hemodialysis: 50 mg once daily; experience is limited, so use with caution (SmPC). About 3% removed by hemodialysis; timing relative to dialysis not critical.

pd.text: SmPC dose for ESKD (50 mg once daily) does not specify modality; no peritoneal dialysis data.

crrt.text: No data in the SmPC. Glucose control in critical illness is usually with insulin.

dialyzable: Minimally: about 3% removed by hemodialysis; the main inactive metabolite (LAY 151) is removed (SmPC 5.2).
monitoring: Liver function tests before starting, every 3 months in the first year and periodically thereafter; stop if aminotransferase stays at 3 times the upper limit of normal or more (SmPC 4.4). Watch for pancreatitis, bullous skin lesions and hypoglycemia with a sulfonylurea or insulin.

pediatric.approved_ages: Not recommended under 18 years; safety and efficacy not established (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; kidney dosing not applicable.
